**NWS and local model guidance point to a high near 69–71°F at Sea-Tac Airport on August 2, 2026, aligning closely with the market’s leading bins (68–69°F at 39.5% and 70–71°F at 42%).** Onshore flow from the Pacific maintains a shallow marine layer that limits daytime heating despite seasonal solar input, while partial morning cloud cover reduces surface insolation before gradual clearing allows modest afternoon warming. 

This setup produces temperatures several degrees below the early-August climatological average of ~75–79°F, consistent with the observed early-morning readings in the upper 50s and the absence of strong downslope or offshore winds. Traders appear to weigh the latest NWS point forecast (69°F) against slight model spread that could push readings into the low 70s if clearing occurs earlier than expected, keeping the two central outcomes nearly even. No major synoptic shifts have altered the outlook in the past 24–48 hours, so sentiment remains anchored to these local thermodynamic and boundary-layer factors.

**Trader sentiment for Manila's August 4 maximum temperature clusters tightly around 28–30°C (combined ~82% probability), reflecting uncertainty in how monsoon-driven cloud cover and rainfall will moderate peak readings.**

PAGASA's extended outlook for Metro Manila shows a forecast high of 31°C on August 4 with 70–100% rain chance, consistent with the southwest monsoon (habagat) pattern that typically produces daytime maxima near 31°C amid frequent showers and thunderstorms. Recent days have followed similar patterns—August 2–3 highs of 31–32°C with widespread convective activity—yet persistent cloudiness and localized downpours often cap actual peaks below model guidance. Historical August climatology supports this range, with average highs around 31°C but high day-to-day variability from tropical moisture and storm tracks. The near-even split between 28°C and 29°C outcomes highlights traders' focus on whether enhanced rainfall or clearer breaks will shift the realized maximum, with official agency updates and real-time observations likely to drive any near-term adjustments.
